title: The appeal of abandoned places
summary_es: La fascinación por los edificios abandonados. Prefijos mis- y un-, y sufijos menos frecuentes (-ship, -ual).
text: Photographs of abandoned buildings have become {{1}} popular online. Part of their appeal is surely the {{2}} of seeing nature reclaim what humans built. A factory that once employed thousands now stands {{3}}, its machinery slowly rusting, while trees push through the roof. Critics argue that such images are {{4}}, since they turn real economic {{5}} into something merely picturesque. Yet for the photographers themselves, the work is often an act of {{6}}: many of these buildings will be demolished within years, and their pictures may be the only {{7}} record that survives. Whether we find the results beautiful or {{8}}, they are hard to ignore.

gaps.explanation_es: Adverbio que modifica al adjetivo «popular»: increasingly = cada vez más.
Tras «the» y antes de «of» va un nombre: verbo + -ion.
«Stand» + adjetivo describe un estado: stands silent, stands empty.
Adjetivo con sentido negativo: mis- (mal) + lead + -ing = engañoso.
«Economic hardship» = penurias económicas. El sufijo -ship forma nombres abstractos; «hardness» sería dureza física.
